I've never owned a Loot bag. So I bought one run, for fifty-one SURVIVOR tokens. Here's what happened.
Loot bag seventy-eight seventy-six. In the Loot Dungeon, your bag is your build. You start the run wearing its exact eight items.
Two ways in. Hold a bag, and you play free every twenty-three hours. No bag? Buy an entry with SURVIVOR tokens, like I did.
By the end, I'd traded the bag's gear for a full tier-one kit and a Katana. A hundred and three potions along the way.

Ninety-three moves. First kill at move three. First collectable beast at move fourteen. I ran from anything twice my level, and ten of my thirteen escapes worked. By move fifty-seven, I was taking down a level fifty-five Tengu. And then came move seventy-one.
Apocalypse Shadow Surtr. A tier-one Brute. One fight took me from two hundred fifty-six HP down to seventy-eight. Today, it's a Mega.
Move ninety-one. One ambush, and two hundred ninety-two HP became seventy. A level seventy-six Poltergeist. Dead at level twenty-six, with three hundred and two gold I never spent.
But I walked out with nine beasts. Three of them are Mega, out of only twenty-two in the whole dungeon. The other six went straight into staking.
Read the bag before you buy the run.
Carry all three weapon types, and switch before you swing.
Platinum Ring for damage. Gold Ring for the kill.
DEX is your escape key. Running is a strategy.
Spend your gold before you explore.
And staking is a bet. Anyone can take a beast while it evolves.
Three days in: five hundred and one runs, and over thirteen hundred beasts collected. My first run? Number seventy-nine.
Your bag is your character. See you in the dungeon.
